newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude diffs idle, Canadian deal seen.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude diffs idle, Canadian deal seen.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices eased with West Texas Intermediate (WTI), while differentials for Alaskan grade stayed idle as a major refinery removed itself from the domestic market by buying a Canadian equivalent Friday, traders said.
Alaska North Slope (ANS) was priced $2.30 off November WTI, with buyers bidding $2.50 under and sellers offering minus $2.10, traders said.
"I'm buying Canadian," one refiner trader said, adding he purchased a 2,000 barrel-per-day parcel of British Columbian light for November delivery on Friday.
November WTI fell five cents from Friday to $25.70/25.80 a barrel. Outright prices for ANS fell in line with WTI, touching $23.30/23.60, or five cents below Friday levels.
Tosco, Ultramar, and Unocal considered scaling back crude processing in early November to cut losses on weak margins.
Traders said weak margins also weakened demand for shipments on California's Line 63. Space restrictions will be announced Tuesday, said ARCO, which runs the Line.
Line 63 crude prices remained $3.20 to $3.00 off November WTI, while California heavy crudes remained flat.
Kern River crude was $17.40/17.60 a barrel, traders said.
